## Explicit S3 correction

The original `s=40 m, lateral=+3.5 m` lands on road 20/lane 2, **Median**.
Live topology at exactly the same longitudinal site shows route lane −1, Driving,
3.5 m wide; its left neighbour is lane 1, Shoulder, 0.5 m wide. Its right neighbour
is lane −2, Driving, 3.5 m wide, same direction and outside any junction.
Therefore only S3's lateral sign changed to **−3.5 m**. The ego route, longitudinal
site, no-stop expectation, thresholds and S1/S2/S4/S5 configurations are unchanged.
The lateral truth probe reads this committed S3 offset instead of duplicating a sign.

Both clean S3 spawns agree exactly. CARLA centre: `(17.1813755, 28.2317734)`;
yaw 0.1591829 degrees. Non-projected lookups confirm the centre and all four footprint
corners on road 20/lane −2, Driving. Core-frame footprint (metres):

| 3 | 14.811709 | −29.306919 |
| 4 | 14.817720 | −27.143476 |

Measured signed lateral extent: **[−4.581725, −2.418274] m**. Ego corridor half-width:

## Packaging and integration

`accepted-20261025.zip` contains the unmodified report/raw callbacks/placements, command
log, topology survey, exact source/scenario/mission bytes and packaging-time working-tree patch.
`accepted-manifest.json` gives the archive SHA256 and each uncompressed member's size/hash.
Verify these against the bytes before reuse. Earlier failed evidence is not overwritten.

Latest main need not be merged to run this standalone verifier: none of its navigation,
mission-loading, world-session or vehicle-adapter dependencies changed on canonical main.
A read-only merge-tree check reports no committed-history conflicts. No actual merge was
performed. Canonical G1 binds the src/config inventory; these additions therefore require
reviewed rebinding before operational/#41 use. The evaluation verifier does not use that
loader, and admission is not weakened or extended here.

The #39 technical verification is complete; approval/publication is still a reviewer action.
This evidence neither admits pedestrian control nor certifies S1–S5 driving acceptance.

The packaging-time patch also includes supporting tests/docs completed after capture;
it is not the capture-time `source_diff_sha256`. The individually hashed source and
configuration snapshots are the authority for the exact executed code. The report's
capture-time diff hash is retained without claiming the later patch reproduces it.
